commits.title: Buy Now on a piece already in the bag hands off that line (restores cb0e434)
commits.forShoppers: If the bag holds only that piece, and a shopper taps Add to cart and then Buy Now on it, checkout opens with 1 piece at full price. Before, it opened with 2 pieces at 15% off. The bag keeps 1. If the bag also holds other pieces, the piece now goes to checkout once, not twice. With the hoops and the bracelet in the bag: before, 3 pieces at 25% off; now, 2 pieces at 15% off. Buy Now on an empty bag, or on a piece the bag does not hold yet, works as before. Also changed: if the bag still shows the piece but Shopify no longer has it (the Shopify cart ran out after some days, or the piece was taken out in another tab), Buy Now now opens checkout with the bag as it shows. Before, the bag was emptied with 'Your cart timed out' and 'Could not open checkout', and checkout did not open. (The fixup d8a943d, with eb25b43 after it, fixes this: Buy Now then puts the piece in again, as many times as the bag showed it, and opens checkout with it.) Also: if the bag shows 2 of a piece and Shopify now has only 1 left, this commit alone opens checkout with the bag's 2 at 15% off, on a Shopify cart that holds 1, with no message. Main opened checkout with 1 at full price and said 'Only 1 of Prism Rivière Bracelet left, all in your bag.' (The fixups d8a943d and c54113c bring that back: checkout gets the 1 Shopify has, and the shopper is told why.)
commits.forMeta: Bracelet alone in the bag (2399): before, AddToCart fired twice (pixel and server each) and InitiateCheckout had value 4798, num_items 2. After, AddToCart fires once and InitiateCheckout has value 2399, num_items 1, content id 47501788348578. With the hoops also in the bag: one AddToCart fewer, and InitiateCheckout goes from value 6097, num_items 3 to 3698, num_items 2. When the Shopify cart is gone but the bag still shows the piece: before, no InitiateCheckout; now one (value 2399, num_items 1), from the pixel and the server. (With the fixup d8a943d, that case also sends one AddToCart, 2399, quantity 1, for the piece put back in; with eb25b43, a bag showing 2 of it sends 4798, quantity 2.)
commits.forCheckout: Bracelet alone in the bag: Fastrr before got products [{47501788348578, qty 2}] with couponCode BUY2; after, [{47501788348578, qty 1}] with no coupon. With the hoops also in the bag: before, [{hoops,1},{bracelet,2}] with BUY3; after, [{hoops,1},{bracelet,1}] with BUY2. The Shopify cart line is no longer raised to 2, and the extra rung code is no longer set. When Shopify no longer has the piece: before, nothing was handed off. Now Fastrr is handed the bag as it shows (Shopify cart gone: [{47501788348578, qty 1}], no coupon), but the Shopify checkout address it gets as its fallback points at a cart Shopify no longer has. With only the bracelet's line gone and the hoops also in the bag, Fastrr gets [{hoops,1},{bracelet,1}] with BUY2 while the Shopify cart holds only the hoops. (The fixup d8a943d fixes this: the piece is first put back on a Shopify cart that holds it; with eb25b43, as many times as the bag showed it.) If Shopify has fewer of the piece left than the bag shows (bag 2, 1 left), this commit alone hands off the bag's 2 with BUY2 on a Shopify cart that holds 1, as the final check measured. With the fixups, Fastrr gets [{47501788348578, qty 1}] with no coupon, as on main.
commits.risk: Low for the shop, but it changes money and Meta counts on this path: no second piece, no Buy 2 / Buy 3 code earned by that second piece, and one AddToCart fewer. Needs the owner's yes (the reviewer held it for that reason). On its own it also skips Shopify's check of that line (see above), so approve it together with the fixup d8a943d, and with 3e6cff9, which that fixup needs. The later fixups on this card, eb25b43, 4f3b3df and c54113c, go with d8a943d.

commits.title: Bag Undo waits for an in-flight removal (restores 2128022)
commits.forShoppers: An Undo tapped straight after Remove brings the piece back, and the rest of the bag stays. Measured with Undo at 300 ms and the removal taking 900 ms. Before: if the Undo reached Shopify first, the hoops were silently lost; if the removal did, the whole bag was wiped as 'timed out'. Also changed, on a line Shopify no longer has (taken out in another tab, say): Remove now says 'Could not remove this item.' and keeps the row (the next commit, f2b05f4, fixes this). Tapping + says 'Could not update quantity.' and keeps the row. Adding that piece again says it couldn't be added, and the row stays (the fixup commit 5bbc08c fixes these two). On main, all three emptied the whole bag; + and Add again also said 'Your cart timed out'. The row goes the next time the bag is opened.
commits.forMeta: Before: if the removal reached Shopify first, the Undo sent no AddToCart, because the add failed and the bag was wiped as 'timed out'. If the Undo reached Shopify first, it sent one AddToCart, for a piece that then vanished. After: the Undo always sends one AddToCart (hoops, 1299) from the pixel and from the server, for a piece that stays in the bag. Also, until f2b05f4 and 5bbc08c: after Remove or + on a line Shopify no longer has, the dead row stays, and the bag's Checkout then sends AddPaymentInfo (value 3143, num_items 2) and InitiateCheckout (value 3698, num_items 2) that count it, from the pixel and the server. On main the bag had been emptied, so neither was sent. Nothing else Meta receives changes.
commits.forCheckout: Shopify cart: before, Remove then 'set the removed line to 2' (or a refusal that wiped the bag); after, Remove then 'add the hoops', and the cart holds both. Checkout then gets what the bag shows (both pieces). Also: after Remove (until f2b05f4), or + or Add again (until 5bbc08c), on a line Shopify no longer has, checkout is still handed that dead row. Measured on this commit alone, applied to main: Fastrr got [{bracelet,1},{hoops,1}] with BUY2 while the Shopify cart held only the bracelet. On main the bag was emptied, so there was nothing to check out.
commits.risk: On its own it leaves the dead-line side effects described above. Approve it together with f2b05f4 (Remove) and the fixup 5bbc08c (+ and Add again), or say no to all three. Reverting the three together at the head c54113c is clean (686 tests pass, types check).

commits.title: A piece Shopify already dropped from the bag: + takes its row out and Add puts it back, instead of emptying the bag
commits.forShoppers: This is for a piece still showing in the bag after Shopify has already dropped it (taken out in another tab, for example). Tapping + (or - above 1) on it now takes that row out, keeps the rest of the bag, and says 'Woven Gold Hoops was no longer in your bag. Please add it again.' On main the whole bag was emptied with 'Your cart timed out'. With the Undo commits alone it said 'Could not update quantity.' and the dead row stayed. Adding that piece again from its page now puts it back in the bag, with no message. On main the whole bag was emptied. With the Undo commits alone it said the piece couldn't be added, and the dead row stayed. If Shopify cannot add it back, the usual 'couldn't be added' message shows and the dead row is gone.
commits.forMeta: Adding the piece again now sends one AddToCart (Woven Gold Hoops, 1299, quantity 1) from the Meta pixel and from the server. Main and the Undo commits alone sent none for it. Checking out after the + now sends AddPaymentInfo (value 2399, num_items 1) and InitiateCheckout (value 2399, num_items 1), the bracelet only, from the pixel and the server. The Undo commits alone sent AddPaymentInfo 3143 and InitiateCheckout 3698, both num_items 2, counting the dead row. On main the bag was empty, so there was no checkout and neither was sent. Checking out after Add again sends the same AddPaymentInfo (3143, 2) and InitiateCheckout (3698, 2) as the Undo commits alone, now for pieces the Shopify cart really holds. Tapping + itself sends nothing, as before.
commits.forCheckout: Measured with the bracelet and the hoops in the bag, after Shopify dropped the hoops. After +, then Checkout: Fastrr gets [{47501788348578, qty 1}] with no coupon. The Undo commits alone gave [{bracelet,1},{hoops,1}] with BUY2 while the Shopify cart held only the bracelet. Main had no bag to check out. After Add again, then Checkout: Fastrr gets [{bracelet,1},{hoops,1}] with BUY2, and the Shopify cart now really holds both (a new hoops line). The Undo commits alone handed over the same two with BUY2, on a Shopify cart holding only the bracelet. The same Shopify cart is kept throughout. A lost cart still empties the bag as before.
commits.risk: Low. It only runs when Shopify says a bag line no longer exists. Add again adds the quantity asked for (1), not the dead row's count plus 1, which matches what Shopify holds and what AddToCart reports. One rare case is not changed here: on the outfit page, Buy Now with 3 picked over a dead row of 1 opens checkout with 2 (before: no checkout); outfits are sold out on the live shop. The other case noted before, Buy Now on a jewellery piece whose row is dead handing off that row, is fixed by the fixup d8a943d. Re-running the other bag cases on the served build gave the same results as before (Undo race both ways, Remove of a dead row, Add then Buy Now, two pieces then Buy Now).

commits.title: Buy Now on a piece already in the bag first checks that Shopify still has it, and puts it back in if not
commits.forShoppers: This is for a piece still showing in the bag after Shopify has lost the bag (the Shopify cart ran out after some days, or was used for an order on Shopify's own checkout) or has dropped that piece (taken out in another tab, say). Buy Now on that piece now puts 1 of it in again and opens checkout with it, with no message. If the bag showed 2 of that piece, checkout opens with 1 at full price and the bag then shows 1; with a working Shopify cart the same tap sends the bag's 2 at 15% off. If Shopify lost the whole bag and the bag held other pieces too, those leave the bag, because Shopify no longer has them. If only that piece was dropped, the rest of the bag stays. On main the bag was emptied, 'Could not open checkout. Please try again.' and 'Your cart timed out. Please add the piece again.' showed, and checkout did not open. With 2b702d9 alone, checkout opened with the bag as it showed (2 at 15% off in the example above), on a Shopify cart that was gone or no longer held the piece. When Shopify still has the piece and enough of it, checkout opens with the piece as the bag holds it, as with 2b702d9, after one answer from Shopify (main waited for one answer here too; 2b702d9 alone skipped it). (The fixup eb25b43 fixes the bag-showed-2 case: the piece then goes back in as many times as the bag showed it, so checkout opens with 2 at 15% off and the bag keeps 2.) If Shopify has fewer of the piece left than the bag shows (the bag shows 2, Shopify has 1, the cart still works), checkout opens with the 1 Shopify has, at full price, and the bag drops to 1, with no message on this commit. Main said 'Only 1 of Prism Rivière Bracelet left, all in your bag.' before opening the same checkout. 2b702d9 alone sent the bag's 2 with BUY2, on a Shopify cart that held 1. (The fixup c54113c brings main's message back, here and when a piece put back in after a lost cart or a dropped line gets fewer than the bag showed.)
commits.forMeta: Measured with Prism Riviere Bracelet (2399). When Shopify no longer has the piece, Buy Now now sends one AddToCart for it (value 2399, quantity 1, content id 47501788348578) from the Meta pixel and from the server, then InitiateCheckout (value 2399, num_items 1). On main neither was sent, because checkout did not open. 2b702d9 alone sent that InitiateCheckout but no AddToCart. If the bag showed 2 of the bracelet, it is the same AddToCart (2399, quantity 1) and InitiateCheckout (2399, num_items 1); 2b702d9 alone sent InitiateCheckout 4798, num_items 2. With the hoops also in the bag and only the bracelet dropped: without 98ca8cb, InitiateCheckout is value 3698, num_items 2, as with 2b702d9 alone, but now for pieces the Shopify cart really holds; with 98ca8cb it is 2399, 1, as before. With the hoops in the bag and the whole Shopify cart gone: one AddToCart (2399, 1), then InitiateCheckout 2399, 1, with or without 98ca8cb. When Shopify still has the piece: nothing changes from 2b702d9 (no AddToCart at Buy Now, the same InitiateCheckout). (With the fixup eb25b43, the bag-showed-2 case sends AddToCart 4798, quantity 2, then InitiateCheckout 4798, num_items 2.) When Shopify has fewer left than the bag shows (bag 2, 1 left, cart working): AddToCart is unchanged (none at Buy Now; main sent one, 2399, quantity 1), and InitiateCheckout is 2399 with 1 item where the bag showed 2, the same as main.
commits.forCheckout: Bracelet alone in the bag, Shopify cart gone: main handed Fastrr nothing. 2b702d9 alone handed [{47501788348578, qty 1}] with a fallback address on the lost cart. Now [{47501788348578, qty 1}], no coupon, with the fallback on a new Shopify cart that holds it. Bracelet shown twice in the bag, Shopify cart gone or its line dropped: Fastrr now gets [{47501788348578, qty 1}] with no coupon (2b702d9 alone: qty 2 with BUY2, on a cart that no longer held it; main: nothing). Hoops and bracelet in the bag, cart gone, Buy Now on the bracelet: the same, with or without 98ca8cb (2b702d9 with 98ca8cb gave the same hand-off but left both pieces in the bag on the lost cart). Bracelet alone, its line dropped: the bracelet is first added back to the bag's own Shopify cart, then the same hand-off, with the fallback on that cart (2b702d9 alone: the same hand-off, on a cart holding nothing). Hoops and bracelet, the bracelet's line dropped: without 98ca8cb, [{hoops,1},{bracelet,1}] with BUY2, and the Shopify cart now really holds both (2b702d9 alone: the same, on a cart holding only the hoops); with 98ca8cb, [{bracelet,1}] on a cart of its own, as before. When Shopify still has the piece, Fastrr gets exactly what 2b702d9 gives it. The Shopify cart gets one extra call at the tap that sets the line to the quantity it already holds (main made one call here too, raising the line to 2). (With the fixup eb25b43, the bracelet shown twice goes to Fastrr as [{47501788348578, qty 2}] with BUY2, on a Shopify cart that holds 2.) When Shopify has fewer left than the bag shows (bag 2, 1 left, cart working): Fastrr gets [{47501788348578, qty 1}] with no coupon and the Shopify cart holds 1, the same as main (2b702d9 alone: qty 2 with BUY2, on a cart holding 1).
commits.risk: Low. It adds one Shopify call before checkout on this path, as main had. If that call fails for another reason (no connection, any other refusal), the line is handed off as it is, as with 2b702d9. Measured on the served build too: checkout opens with the bracelet (2399, 1 item), with no AddToCart and no message. On main the same refusal showed 'Could not open checkout. Please try again.' and 'Prism Rivière Bracelet couldn't be added. Please try again.', and checkout did not open. When Shopify has lost the whole bag, the other pieces now leave the bag at the Buy Now tap. Main emptied the whole bag; with 2b702d9 and 98ca8cb they stayed, on a cart Shopify no longer had. Not changed here: on the outfit page, Buy Now with more picked than a dropped row held (3 over 1) still opens checkout with the difference (2); outfits are sold out on the live shop.

commits.title: Buy Now puts a piece back in as many times as the bag showed it, when Shopify had lost it
commits.forShoppers: This is for a piece the bag shows more than once (2, say, after + in the bag) when Shopify has lost the bag or dropped that piece. Buy Now on it now puts it back in as many times as the bag showed, so checkout opens with 2 at 15% off and the bag still shows 2, the same as with a working Shopify cart. With d8a943d alone, checkout opened with 1 at full price, with no message, and the bag then showed 1. With 2b702d9 alone checkout also got 2 at 15% off, but on a Shopify cart that no longer held them. On main checkout did not open. Nothing changes when the bag shows the piece once, or when Shopify still has it. If Shopify has fewer of the piece left than the bag showed (bag 2, 1 left), the piece goes back with the 1 Shopify has, checkout opens with that at full price and the bag shows 1; on this commit that happens with no message (the fixup c54113c adds 'Only 1 of Prism Rivière Bracelet left, all in your bag.').
commits.forMeta: Measured with Prism Riviere Bracelet (2399) shown twice in the bag. When Shopify has lost the cart or dropped the line, the AddToCart for the piece put back now says quantity 2, value 4798 (d8a943d alone: quantity 1, 2399), from the Meta pixel and from the server. InitiateCheckout is then value 4798, num_items 2 (d8a943d alone: 2399, 1; 2b702d9 alone: 4798, 2, with no AddToCart). With the hoops also in the bag and only the bracelet dropped: without 98ca8cb, InitiateCheckout 6097, num_items 3 (d8a943d alone: 3698, 2); with 98ca8cb, 4798, 2 (d8a943d alone: 2399, 1). With the hoops too and the whole Shopify cart gone: 4798, 2, with or without 98ca8cb. The + tap in the bag sends no AddToCart, so Meta hears an AddToCart of 1 at Add and one of 2 at this Buy Now. Nothing changes when the bag shows the piece once, or when Shopify still has it. If Shopify has fewer left than the bag showed (bag 2, 1 left, cart gone or line dropped): AddToCart still says quantity 2 (4798) although Shopify kept 1, then InitiateCheckout 2399, 1 item (measured; c54113c does not change either).
commits.forCheckout: Bracelet shown twice in the bag. Shopify cart gone: Fastrr now gets [{47501788348578, qty 2}] with BUY2, on a new Shopify cart that holds 2 and the BUY2 code (d8a943d alone: qty 1, no coupon). Its line dropped: the bracelet goes back on the bag's own Shopify cart as a new line of 2, and Fastrr gets the same (d8a943d alone: a line of 1, qty 1, no coupon). Hoops in the bag too, the bracelet's line dropped: without 98ca8cb, [{hoops,1},{bracelet,2}] with BUY3, and the Shopify cart holds both (d8a943d alone: [{hoops,1},{bracelet,1}] with BUY2); with 98ca8cb, [{bracelet,2}] with BUY2 on a cart of its own (d8a943d alone: [{bracelet,1}], no coupon). Hoops too and the whole cart gone: [{bracelet,2}] with BUY2, with or without 98ca8cb (d8a943d alone: [{bracelet,1}], no coupon), because the hoops left the bag with the lost cart. In every case except that last one without 98ca8cb, this is what a working Shopify cart hands off for the same bag. In that one case a working cart hands off [{hoops,1},{bracelet,2}] with BUY3. The fallback address carries the same code. Unchanged, re-measured on the served builds: the piece shown once (cart gone, line dropped, two pieces, Add then Buy Now, empty bag, a failed check), the outfit page, and + or Add again on a dropped line. If Shopify has fewer left than the bag showed (bag 2, 1 left, cart gone or line dropped): Fastrr gets [{47501788348578, qty 1}] with no coupon and the Shopify cart holds 1 (unchanged by c54113c).
commits.risk: Low. It only runs when Shopify has lost the bag or dropped the piece and the bag showed it more than once, and it puts back what the bag showed. That earns the Buy 2 / Buy 3 code a working cart would have earned, with one exception: other pieces in the bag, the whole Shopify cart gone, and 98ca8cb refused. There the other pieces have left the bag, so checkout gets Buy 2 on the 2 bracelets, where a working cart gives Buy 3 on all 3 pieces. Also measured: if Shopify has fewer of the piece left than the bag showed (bag showed 2, cart gone, 1 left), checkout opens with 1 at full price and the bag then shows 1, with no message. AddToCart still says quantity 2 (4798), while InitiateCheckout says 2399, 1 item. Reverting it alone at 4f3b3df was clean (689 tests pass) and gave back d8a943d's way. At the new head c54113c, which changes two of its lines, revert c54113c with it: clean, 689 tests pass, types check, and d8a943d's way comes back.

commits.title: Buy Now on a piece already in the bag hands off that line (restores cb0e434)
commits.forShoppers: If the bag holds only that piece, and a shopper taps Add to cart and then Buy Now on it, checkout opens with 1 piece at full price. Before, it opened with 2 pieces at 15% off. The bag keeps 1. If the bag also holds other pieces, the piece now goes to checkout once, not twice. With the hoops and the bracelet in the bag: before, 3 pieces at 25% off; now, 2 pieces at 15% off. Buy Now on an empty bag, or on a piece the bag does not hold yet, works as before. Also changed: if the bag still shows the piece but Shopify no longer has it (the Shopify cart ran out after some days, or the piece was taken out in another tab), Buy Now now opens checkout with the bag as it shows. Before, the bag was emptied with 'Your cart timed out' and 'Could not open checkout', and checkout did not open. (The fixup d8a943d, with eb25b43 after it, fixes this: Buy Now then puts the piece in again, as many times as the bag showed it, and opens checkout with it.) Also: if the bag shows 2 of a piece and Shopify now has only 1 left, this commit alone opens checkout with the bag's 2 at 15% off, on a Shopify cart that holds 1, with no message. Main opened checkout with 1 at full price and said 'Only 1 of Prism Rivière Bracelet left, all in your bag.' (The fixups d8a943d and c54113c bring that back: checkout gets the 1 Shopify has, and the shopper is told why.)
commits.forMeta: Bracelet alone in the bag (2399): before, AddToCart fired twice (pixel and server each) and InitiateCheckout had value 4798, num_items 2. After, AddToCart fires once and InitiateCheckout has value 2399, num_items 1, content id 47501788348578. With the hoops also in the bag: one AddToCart fewer, and InitiateCheckout goes from value 6097, num_items 3 to 3698, num_items 2. When the Shopify cart is gone but the bag still shows the piece: before, no InitiateCheckout; now one (value 2399, num_items 1), from the pixel and the server. (With the fixup d8a943d, that case also sends one AddToCart, 2399, quantity 1, for the piece put back in; with eb25b43, a bag showing 2 of it sends 4798, quantity 2.)
commits.forCheckout: Bracelet alone in the bag: Fastrr before got products [{47501788348578, qty 2}] with couponCode BUY2; after, [{47501788348578, qty 1}] with no coupon. With the hoops also in the bag: before, [{hoops,1},{bracelet,2}] with BUY3; after, [{hoops,1},{bracelet,1}] with BUY2. The Shopify cart line is no longer raised to 2, and the extra rung code is no longer set. When Shopify no longer has the piece: before, nothing was handed off. Now Fastrr is handed the bag as it shows (Shopify cart gone: [{47501788348578, qty 1}], no coupon), but the Shopify checkout address it gets as its fallback points at a cart Shopify no longer has. With only the bracelet's line gone and the hoops also in the bag, Fastrr gets [{hoops,1},{bracelet,1}] with BUY2 while the Shopify cart holds only the hoops. (The fixup d8a943d fixes this: the piece is first put back on a Shopify cart that holds it; with eb25b43, as many times as the bag showed it.) If Shopify has fewer of the piece left than the bag shows (bag 2, 1 left), this commit alone hands off the bag's 2 with BUY2 on a Shopify cart that holds 1, as the final check measured. With the fixups, Fastrr gets [{47501788348578, qty 1}] with no coupon, as on main.

commits.forShoppers: An Undo tapped straight after Remove brings the piece back, and the rest of the bag stays. Measured with Undo at 300 ms and the removal taking 900 ms. Before: if the Undo reached Shopify first, the hoops were silently lost; if the removal did, the whole bag was wiped as 'timed out'. Also changed, on a line Shopify no longer has (taken out in another tab, say): Remove now says 'Could not remove this item.' and keeps the row (the next commit, f2b05f4, fixes this). Tapping + says 'Could not update quantity.' and keeps the row. Adding that piece again says it couldn't be added, and the row stays (the fixup commit 5bbc08c fixes these two). On main, all three emptied the whole bag; + and Add again also said 'Your cart timed out'. The row goes the next time the bag is opened.
commits.forMeta: Before: if the removal reached Shopify first, the Undo sent no AddToCart, because the add failed and the bag was wiped as 'timed out'. If the Undo reached Shopify first, it sent one AddToCart, for a piece that then vanished. After: the Undo always sends one AddToCart (hoops, 1299) from the pixel and from the server, for a piece that stays in the bag. Also, until f2b05f4 and 5bbc08c: after Remove or + on a line Shopify no longer has, the dead row stays, and the bag's Checkout then sends AddPaymentInfo (value 3143, num_items 2) and InitiateCheckout (value 3698, num_items 2) that count it, from the pixel and the server. On main the bag had been emptied, so neither was sent. Nothing else Meta receives changes.
commits.forCheckout: Shopify cart: before, Remove then 'set the removed line to 2' (or a refusal that wiped the bag); after, Remove then 'add the hoops', and the cart holds both. Checkout then gets what the bag shows (both pieces). Also: after Remove (until f2b05f4), or + or Add again (until 5bbc08c), on a line Shopify no longer has, checkout is still handed that dead row. Measured on this commit alone, applied to main: Fastrr got [{bracelet,1},{hoops,1}] with BUY2 while the Shopify cart held only the bracelet. On main the bag was emptied, so there was nothing to check out.
commits.risk: On its own it leaves the dead-line side effects described above. Approve it together with f2b05f4 (Remove) and the fixup 5bbc08c (+ and Add again), or say no to all three. Reverting the three together at the head c54113c is clean (686 tests pass, types check).

commits.title: Buy Now on a piece already in the bag first checks that Shopify still has it, and puts it back in if not
commits.forShoppers: This is for a piece still showing in the bag after Shopify has lost the bag (the Shopify cart ran out after some days, or was used for an order on Shopify's own checkout) or has dropped that piece (taken out in another tab, say). Buy Now on that piece now puts 1 of it in again and opens checkout with it, with no message. If the bag showed 2 of that piece, checkout opens with 1 at full price and the bag then shows 1; with a working Shopify cart the same tap sends the bag's 2 at 15% off. If Shopify lost the whole bag and the bag held other pieces too, those leave the bag, because Shopify no longer has them. If only that piece was dropped, the rest of the bag stays. On main the bag was emptied, 'Could not open checkout. Please try again.' and 'Your cart timed out. Please add the piece again.' showed, and checkout did not open. With 2b702d9 alone, checkout opened with the bag as it showed (2 at 15% off in the example above), on a Shopify cart that was gone or no longer held the piece. When Shopify still has the piece and enough of it, checkout opens with the piece as the bag holds it, as with 2b702d9, after one answer from Shopify (main waited for one answer here too; 2b702d9 alone skipped it). (The fixup eb25b43 fixes the bag-showed-2 case: the piece then goes back in as many times as the bag showed it, so checkout opens with 2 at 15% off and the bag keeps 2.) If Shopify has fewer of the piece left than the bag shows (the bag shows 2, Shopify has 1, the cart still works), checkout opens with the 1 Shopify has, at full price, and the bag drops to 1, with no message on this commit. Main said 'Only 1 of Prism Rivière Bracelet left, all in your bag.' before opening the same checkout. 2b702d9 alone sent the bag's 2 with BUY2, on a Shopify cart that held 1. (The fixup c54113c brings main's message back, here and when a piece put back in after a lost cart or a dropped line gets fewer than the bag showed.)
commits.forMeta: Measured with Prism Riviere Bracelet (2399). When Shopify no longer has the piece, Buy Now now sends one AddToCart for it (value 2399, quantity 1, content id 47501788348578) from the Meta pixel and from the server, then InitiateCheckout (value 2399, num_items 1). On main neither was sent, because checkout did not open. 2b702d9 alone sent that InitiateCheckout but no AddToCart. If the bag showed 2 of the bracelet, it is the same AddToCart (2399, quantity 1) and InitiateCheckout (2399, num_items 1); 2b702d9 alone sent InitiateCheckout 4798, num_items 2. With the hoops also in the bag and only the bracelet dropped: without 98ca8cb, InitiateCheckout is value 3698, num_items 2, as with 2b702d9 alone, but now for pieces the Shopify cart really holds; with 98ca8cb it is 2399, 1, as before. With the hoops in the bag and the whole Shopify cart gone: one AddToCart (2399, 1), then InitiateCheckout 2399, 1, with or without 98ca8cb. When Shopify still has the piece: nothing changes from 2b702d9 (no AddToCart at Buy Now, the same InitiateCheckout). (With the fixup eb25b43, the bag-showed-2 case sends AddToCart 4798, quantity 2, then InitiateCheckout 4798, num_items 2.) When Shopify has fewer left than the bag shows (bag 2, 1 left, cart working): AddToCart is unchanged (none at Buy Now; main sent one, 2399, quantity 1), and InitiateCheckout is 2399 with 1 item where the bag showed 2, the same as main.
commits.forCheckout: Bracelet alone in the bag, Shopify cart gone: main handed Fastrr nothing. 2b702d9 alone handed [{47501788348578, qty 1}] with a fallback address on the lost cart. Now [{47501788348578, qty 1}], no coupon, with the fallback on a new Shopify cart that holds it. Bracelet shown twice in the bag, Shopify cart gone or its line dropped: Fastrr now gets [{47501788348578, qty 1}] with no coupon (2b702d9 alone: qty 2 with BUY2, on a cart that no longer held it; main: nothing). Hoops and bracelet in the bag, cart gone, Buy Now on the bracelet: the same, with or without 98ca8cb (2b702d9 with 98ca8cb gave the same hand-off but left both pieces in the bag on the lost cart). Bracelet alone, its line dropped: the bracelet is first added back to the bag's own Shopify cart, then the same hand-off, with the fallback on that cart (2b702d9 alone: the same hand-off, on a cart holding nothing). Hoops and bracelet, the bracelet's line dropped: without 98ca8cb, [{hoops,1},{bracelet,1}] with BUY2, and the Shopify cart now really holds both (2b702d9 alone: the same, on a cart holding only the hoops); with 98ca8cb, [{bracelet,1}] on a cart of its own, as before. When Shopify still has the piece, Fastrr gets exactly what 2b702d9 gives it. The Shopify cart gets one extra call at the tap that sets the line to the quantity it already holds (main made one call here too, raising the line to 2). (With the fixup eb25b43, the bracelet shown twice goes to Fastrr as [{47501788348578, qty 2}] with BUY2, on a Shopify cart that holds 2.) When Shopify has fewer left than the bag shows (bag 2, 1 left, cart working): Fastrr gets [{47501788348578, qty 1}] with no coupon and the Shopify cart holds 1, the same as main (2b702d9 alone: qty 2 with BUY2, on a cart holding 1).
commits.risk: Low. It adds one Shopify call before checkout on this path, as main had. If that call fails for another reason (no connection, any other refusal), the line is handed off as it is, as with 2b702d9. Measured on the served build too: checkout opens with the bracelet (2399, 1 item), with no AddToCart and no message. On main the same refusal showed 'Could not open checkout. Not changed here: on the outfit page, Buy Now with more picked than a dropped row held (3 over 1) still opens checkout with the difference (2); outfits are sold out on the live shop.

commits.title: Bag lines take Shopify's current price on every cart answer
commits.ownerQuestion: Do you accept that the checkout value Meta receives (the checkout start and the payment step) follows Shopify's current price, not the price the page showed when the piece was added? The bag Total then always matches what you charge. Undo in the bag also puts a piece back at Shopify's price. Approve or decline together with 780534a, as one item.
commits.forShoppers: The bag's line prices, its Total and the Buy 2 / Buy 3 saving now always match what checkout charges. Before: a saved bag holding Mesh Band Ring at ₹699 showed ₹699 and a Total of ₹699, while Shopify charges ₹799. After: ₹799, Total ₹799. Heartline added from an out-of-date card at ₹2,449 showed ₹2,449 before and ₹1,899 after. Undo after removing a piece puts it back at ₹799 (it was ₹699). A signed-in member's account history also records Shopify's price for a started checkout. That last point comes from reading the code; it was not measured.
commits.forMeta: The checkout value Meta gets (InitiateCheckout) and its item price now follow Shopify's price, not the price the page showed at the tap. So does the payment-step value (AddPaymentInfo). The browser pixel and the server copy change together and still share one event id. Add to cart from a product page or card keeps the page's price. One exception: Undo after removing a piece in the bag re-adds it at the bag's price, which is now Shopify's. ViewContent is unchanged. Measured before → after: on the out-of-date bag, AddPaymentInfo 699→799 and InitiateCheckout value and item price 699→799. For Heartline, AddPaymentInfo 2449→1899 and InitiateCheckout 2449→1899, with Add to cart staying at 2449. Undo on the out-of-date bag sent Add to cart 699→799, browser pixel and server copy.
commits.forCheckout: No change. Shiprocket was handed the same pieces before and after: Mesh Band Ring (Gold, size 6) at quantity 1 and Heartline at quantity 1, with no code and the same fallback link. Shiprocket is never sent prices. The pieces in Shopify's cart do not change; Shopify is only read for its prices. In the Undo run nothing was handed over either way.
commits.risk: Low. If Shopify's answer has no price, the line keeps the price it has. The bag uses Shopify's price before discounts and works out the Buy 2 / Buy 3 saving itself. For Meta, three things change and you must accept them: the checkout value, the payment-step value, and the Add to cart sent when Undo puts a piece back in the bag. Nothing is changed in your Shopify admin.

With 780534a, applied alone on main, tsc passes and 650/650 tests pass (review run, and the F1 folded tree here).

commits.ownerQuestion: Is it OK to stop telling Meta about Add to cart taps that added nothing because the last piece was already in the bag, and to count 1 instead of 2 when only 1 more could be added?
commits.forShoppers: No visible change. The bag still keeps 1 and says 'Only 1 of Woven Gold Hoops left, all in your bag'. Buy Now still goes to checkout with the bag as it is.
commits.forMeta: Add to cart is sent only for the pieces Shopify really added, with that quantity and its value. The count is the bag line's quantity after the add, less what the bag held before, and never more than was asked for. The event id and the server copy work as before. Measured with 1 piece left (Add, Add again, Buy Now): before, 3 Add to cart events of 1,299 each (browser pixel and server copy); after, 1. With a piece Shopify answers at 0 (Buy Now on a sold-out ring, this commit alone): before, Add to cart 1,599; after, none. With C25 approved, such a line is refused one step earlier as 'couldn't be added', and the two never both act on one add.
commits.forCheckout: No change. The checkout start (1,299, 1 piece) and the hand-off to Shiprocket (Woven Gold Hoops at quantity 1, no code) were identical before and after. On its own, this commit still lets Buy Now hand a sold-out piece over at quantity 0; C25 is what stops that.
commits.risk: Low. Only when Add to cart is sent, and with what quantity, changes. What the bag does and how Buy Now runs are unchanged. The Add to cart value still uses the price the tap carried: the page's price, or the bag line's price for Undo.

The duplicate 'checkout started' (InitiateCheckout) cannot be merged in code. The second copy comes from another sender, very likely Shiprocket (read from Meta's data, not confirmed in Shiprocket), and that sender never sees our event id. Which one should Meta hear?
(a) Ours, sent at the Checkout tap. It covers both the Shiprocket and the Shopify checkout. You would switch the other one off in Shiprocket's Meta settings, if Shiprocket offers that switch.
(b) The other sender's, sent on its own page. Many of these carry the buyer's email and phone, so Meta matches them better. But it misses the Shopify fallback and anyone whose Shiprocket page fails to load. This needs a small code change on our side.
I recommend (a). The Fastrr plan also asked for ours to keep firing.

commits.forShoppers: Nothing changes. The page, the colour it opens on, its price and what goes into the bag are the same. Only the moment the product view reaches Meta changes, on a few links.
commits.forMeta:
On the published site, product pages are pre-drawn with Shopify's own colours and sizes, so the C19 change already makes Star Point Band's Silver ad and Silver links name Silver US 6 at ₹799 there. This fix changes nothing for Star Point Band on the published site. It matters where a page's stored copy lacks the colour or item a link names. Measured on built pages, iPhone 13 and Pixel 7, landing cold, browser and server copy alike:
- Aquarelle Rivière Bracelet, with today's published pre-drawn page (made before White and Pink were added): the White and Pink ads and the White and Pink links used to report Royal Blue (50714620100770). They now report White (50749309649058) or Pink (50749309681826), the colour on screen and in the bag, at the same ₹1,299. It is the only published page whose stored copy lacks a colour Shopify sells today (all 136 checked). Each publish redraws the product pages from Shopify, so the publish that ships this also gives Aquarelle a pre-drawn page with White and Pink, and the C19 change alone then names them at once (measured). After that, this fix covers any colour or size added in Shopify after the latest publish, until the next one.
- A page opened without its pre-drawn copy (a page the publish could not pre-draw; previews send nothing to Meta): Star Point Band's Silver ad and Silver links go from Gold US 6 (47501788774562) at ₹999 to Silver US 6 (50652105605282) at ₹799. Its Gold link and its Gold US 5, 7 and 8 ads keep the Gold US 6 item, but its value goes from ₹999 to ₹799.
- A link naming a colour the piece is not sold in now waits for Shopify and reports Shopify's price. On the published site that price is already in the pre-drawn page, so only the timing changes (Molten Bloom Hoops ?colour=rose: ₹1,300 before and after, sent about half a second later). Without the pre-drawn copy, it went from ₹2,949 to ₹1,300.
- These views go out once Shopify answers: about 1 second after landing in the test (0.6 to 1.8 s), likely later on a slow phone connection. If Shopify has not answered within 3 seconds, the view goes out then, naming the stored item at the stored price, as before. If the shopper first picks a colour the page already shows, the view goes out at that moment and names that colour (Aquarelle's White ad on today's published page, Lavender picked at 1 s while Shopify was held: Lavender, 50714620133538, ₹1,299, where ddb72b7 reported Royal Blue). If the shopper leaves, switches away or moves to another page first, the view goes out at that moment. If that move is to another page of the shop, the server copy names the new page as the page viewed, not this piece's page. The optional page-address fix (ac7de45) keeps this piece's page instead.
- Still one product view per piece. Every other link sends it at once, as before.
commits.forCheckout: Unchanged. Measured on Pixel 7, ddb72b7, f7d43e9 and this commit alike. The Aquarelle White ad, on today's pre-drawn page: Add to cart puts White (50749309649058) x1 in the Shopify cart, and Buy Now hands Shiprocket White x1 with no code. The Star Point Band Silver ad, without its pre-drawn copy: Add to cart and Buy Now carry Silver US 6 (50652105605282) x1. The 'added to cart' and 'checkout started' events name the same item and price in all three builds (White ₹1,299, Silver ₹799).

commits.forMeta:
Only the page address in Meta's server copy changes, for a product view that was still waiting for Shopify when the shopper moved to another page of the shop or picked another colour. Measured on built pages, iPhone 13 and Pixel 7, Shopify held 6 seconds:
- Star Point Band's Silver ad, opened without its pre-drawn copy, then a tap on Woven Gold Hoops at 1.2 s: the view (Gold US 6, 47501788774562, ₹999, sent at about 1.33 s) used to name Woven Gold Hoops' page. - The same for an in-app move to Prism Rivière Bracelet at 1 s and a tap on Shop All at 1.2 s.
- On the published site today: Aquarelle Rivière Bracelet's White ad, then a tap on Rivière Eternal Necklace: the view used to name the necklace's page. It now names the Aquarelle ad link.
- On the published site today: Aquarelle Rivière Bracelet's White ad, with Lavender picked at 1 s: the view (Lavender, 50714620133538, ₹1,299) used to name the ad link with the Lavender choice added to it. It now names the ad link as the shopper opened it.

- The browser copy's page address comes from Meta's own script, not from the site. Which address it gives could not be checked here, because the script must not load.
commits.forCheckout: Unchanged. Only the product view is touched. Add to cart, Buy Now, the bag and the hand-off to Shopify and Shiprocket are not changed.
commits.risk: Low. Only a product view that waited for Shopify gets this. Every other event still reports the address at the moment it is sent, as before. If the shopper picks another colour during the wait, the view names the colour on screen and the server copy gives the link the page was opened on, as the old first-paint view did. It is built on top of 'Meta's server copy only reports from the real shop': it can only be added after that one, and if both are taken, taking that one back later means taking this one back first.

commits.title: Old Shopify addresses land on their real pages, query kept (owner review)
commits.forShoppers: 23 kinds of old Shopify address that showed 'Coming soon' now open a real page, with the ad's tracking kept. A piece opened from a collection (/collections/bracelets/products/prism-riviere-bracelet?fbclid=…) opens the Prism product page; a piece that is no longer listed, opened the same way, opens the jewellery. The store's old pages: about-naira and about-us go to the homepage; made-for-you and custom go to the outfits page; privacy-policy, terms, exchange-return-policy, gifting and concepts each open their own page; shop opens the jewellery; contact-us opens Contact; faq opens FAQs; size-guide opens the ring size guide article; track-order and /apps/track open Track Order. /cart, /cart/add, /search and /checkout open the jewellery. The shipping, contact and legal policy links open FAQs, Contact and Terms. /collections/dusk and /collections/frontpage open the outfits page instead of the jewellery. Other old collections (/collections/sets) still go to the jewellery but now keep ?fbclid/utm. Truly unknown addresses, and Shopify cart links such as /cart/<number>:1, still show Coming soon. On its own, this commit also sends Shopify's customer-account links (/account/login, /account/register, /account/orders/123, /account/reset/…, /account/activate/…) to the Inner Circle member sign-in, which cannot show an order. Its fixup 4e1c19e takes that out, so with both commits those links keep showing Coming soon, as on main.
commits.forMeta: Measured on main and on this branch. On main, each address that showed Coming soon sent 1 PageView, on that address. Here, a piece opened from a collection sends 1 PageView on the real product address plus 1 ViewContent (browser and server copy: content id 47501788348578, value 2399 INR); main sent no ViewContent. Every other redirected address now sends 2 PageViews instead of 1: one on the old address as it loads, one on the page it lands on (for example /pages/gifting, then /gifting). /collections/dusk, /collections/frontpage and /collections/sets already sent 2 on main, the second on /jewellery with the click id dropped. Here that second PageView is on /customize (dusk, frontpage) or /jewellery (sets), with ?fbclid/utm kept. skipped.why: Not done, because it cannot be done cleanly here. Google's merchant listings do not accept a price-range offer (AggregateOffer). The form they support is a product group with one product per variant. That changes the top-level product data on the 21 multi-variant product pages, and the Meta pixel's automatic Microdata event reads exactly that data. The effect on what Meta receives cannot be measured, because Meta's script cannot be loaded in tests.
